notices.resources/irs/LICENSES.md:
# Factory impulse responses — provenance and licences

**Status: four impulse responses are bundled with Crypta, and every one of them
was generated by this repository rather than recorded by anyone.** That is the
whole licensing argument, and it is deliberately the simplest one available.

> **These are models, not captures.** Nothing in this folder is a recording of
> any cabinet, speaker or microphone. Each file is computed by
> [`tools/ir-synth/cabsynth.py`](../../tools/ir-synth/cabsynth.py) from a
> published analytical model — a cascade of standard analog-prototype filter
> sections plus reflection taps derived from physical path lengths. They are
> voiced from the documented behaviour of moving-coil loudspeakers in boxes, and
> their display names all begin with **"Modelled"** so that a user reading a
> preset list is never left thinking otherwise.

## Why generated rather than sourced

Bundling a cabinet IR means redistributing a recording inside every copy of an
AGPLv3 binary. A capture carries rights from the cabinet, from the microphone,
and from whoever pressed record; third-party packs routinely misstate all three,
and "free download" is not a licence. Sourcing one that clears that bar is a
research project with an uncertain answer.

A generated IR has no such question. There is no third-party recording in it, so
there is nothing to trace, nothing to dispute, and no licensor to find. The
generator is committed alongside the audio: run it, get byte-identical output,
compare the SHA-256 below. **Reproducibility is the provenance.**

## The bar (enforced in code)

Crypta accepts only three licence categories, and
[`src/dsp/FactoryIRs.cpp`](../../src/dsp/FactoryIRs.cpp) drops any asset that
does not name one *and* a checkable source:

| Licence string | Meaning | What must be recorded |
|---|---|---|
| `CC0-1.0` | Creative Commons Zero — dedicated to the public domain | Where it came from, and the date |
| `Public Domain` | An explicit public-domain dedication that is not CC0 | The wording of the dedication and where it is published |
| `Self-recorded` | Captured by this project on gear we own | Cab, speaker, mic, position, date, engineer |

Explicitly **not** accepted:

- "free download", "free for commercial use", "royalty free" — not licences, and
  none of them grants redistribution inside a binary.
- CC-BY / CC-BY-SA — usable, but they carry attribution (and, for SA,
  share-alike) obligations into every downstream copy. Taking that on is a
  deliberate decision for the project owner, not a default.
- Anything whose origin cannot be traced to a named licensor. "It was on a forum"
  is not provenance.

The bundled set is filed under **`CC0-1.0`**, not `Self-recorded`, because
`Self-recorded` means a *capture* and these are not captures — calling them one
would be the exact mislabelling this file exists to prevent. Yves Vogl, as the
author of the generator and therefore of its output, dedicates these four files
to the public domain under CC0 1.0 Universal; the full legal code is committed
next to them in [`CC0-1.0.txt`](CC0-1.0.txt), retrieved from
<https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/legalcode.txt>. The `source`
field of each asset in
[`CryptaAudioProcessor::getFactoryIRAssetTable()`](../../src/PluginProcessor.cpp)
names the generator and the model id, both of which a reviewer can check without
asking anyone.

## Attribution

None is required — CC0 waives it. Nothing in this folder obliges a downstream
user of a Crypta binary to credit anybody, which is the point.

## Bundled impulse responses

All four are mono, 24-bit PCM, 48 kHz, normalised so that the maximum of the
magnitude response is exactly 0 dBFS (so no sine at any frequency can leave the
convolver hotter than it entered it).

| File | Display name | Licence | Samples | Length | SHA-256 (first 16) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `modelled_8x10_cone.wav` | Modelled 8x10 Cone | CC0-1.0 | 4096 | 85.3 ms | `67aa93d0e238e88b` |
| `modelled_8x10_edge.wav` | Modelled 8x10 Edge | CC0-1.0 | 4096 | 85.3 ms | `551d27888c679e86` |
| `modelled_1x15_vintage.wav` | Modelled 1x15 Vintage | CC0-1.0 | 4096 | 85.3 ms | `fd7de6a4fbe4e1fe` |
| `modelled_4x10_horn.wav` | Modelled 4x10 Horn | CC0-1.0 | 4096 | 85.3 ms | `b7e98317d45a340c` |

Full checksums, every filter section, every reflection path length and the exact
generator hash are recorded in [`manifest.json`](manifest.json), which
`tools/ir-synth/verify_irs.py --expect-manifest` re-checks against the audio in
CI — so this record cannot drift away from the files it describes.

### Modelled 8x10 Cone

- **File** `modelled_8x10_cone.wav`, mono, 24-bit PCM, 48 kHz, 4096 samples (85.3 ms)
- **Models** a sealed 8x10 bass stack with a generic cardioid dynamic on the dust
  cap at 2 cm: an under-damped second-order box alignment at 55 Hz, the 10" cone's
  upper-mid growl at 700 Hz and 1.5 kHz, its breakup null at 2.6 kHz, a 24 dB/oct
  inductance roll-off from 4 kHz, plus baffle-edge and floor reflections at 26 cm
  and 55 cm of excess path.
- **Generated by** `tools/ir-synth/cabsynth.py`, model id `bass-810-cone`
- **Licence** CC0-1.0 (dedicated by Yves Vogl, Basilica Audio, 2026-08-22)
- **SHA-256** `67aa93d0e238e88b74b455c3b5322d455d61c007620ace2d2cb88b54c6a793e2`

### Modelled 8x10 Edge

- **File** `modelled_8x10_edge.wav`, mono, 24-bit PCM, 48 kHz, 4096 samples (85.3 ms)
- **Models** the same sealed 8x10 with the microphone moved to the cone edge and
  angled off-axis: a −6 dB high-shelf from 2.5 kHz and one extra low-pass pole
  for the cone's directivity, and +2 dB at 220 Hz for the low-mid the edge
  position picks up. The intended partner for a cone/edge A/B.
- **Generated by** `tools/ir-synth/cabsynth.py`, model id `bass-810-edge`
- **Licence** CC0-1.0 (dedicated by Yves Vogl, Basilica Audio, 2026-08-22)
- **SHA-256** `551d27888c679e864342d70a76c0298a8dbbaf21cb33b81ed995f387bf63a1c3`

### Modelled 1x15 Vintage

- **File** `modelled_1x15_vintage.wav`, mono, 24-bit PCM, 48 kHz, 4096 samples (85.3 ms)
- **Models** a ported 1x15 with a dark vintage voicing and a generic ribbon
  microphone at 5 cm: a fourth-order vented alignment tuned around 45 Hz, the
  15" cone's early breakup and death above 2.2 kHz, and the ribbon's strong
  proximity rise with no presence peak at all.
- **Generated by** `tools/ir-synth/cabsynth.py`, model id `bass-115-vintage`
- **Licence** CC0-1.0 (dedicated by Yves Vogl, Basilica Audio, 2026-08-22)
- **SHA-256** `fd7de6a4fbe4e1fe6a820b657a2dc5e6693db74236ef668c23374d7eee8182e4`

### Modelled 4x10 Horn

- **File** `modelled_4x10_horn.wav`, mono, 24-bit PCM, 48 kHz, 4096 samples (85.3 ms)
- **Models** a ported 4x10 with an HF horn on a passive crossover — the modern,
  extended-top bass voicing. Two parallel paths: a woofer path low-passed at
  24 dB/oct from 3 kHz, and a horn path high-passed at 24 dB/oct from 3.5 kHz,
  at 0.5 gain and delayed by 4 samples because a horn's acoustic centre sits
  behind the woofer baffle plane. That offset is what makes the crossover region
  comb the way a real one does.
- **Generated by** `tools/ir-synth/cabsynth.py`, model id `bass-410-horn`
- **Licence** CC0-1.0 (dedicated by Yves Vogl, Basilica Audio, 2026-08-22)
- **SHA-256** `b7e98317d45a340cff6853392a1fde3bcf4f446a6a7e5f7a0336dabeca1537f4`

## Verified measurements

Measured by `tools/ir-synth/verify_irs.py` from the shipped files, not from the
code that wrote them. Corners are read off a 1/3-octave RMS-smoothed magnitude
response, because a cabinet response is a comb of narrow breakup peaks and
walking outwards from a raw-spectrum maximum measures the skirt of one peak
rather than the cabinet's bandwidth.

| File | peak dBFS | RMS dBFS | max\|H(f)\| | DC rel. peak | −10 dB band | RT (T20) | last sample |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `modelled_8x10_cone.wav` | −18.38 | −47.86 | 0.000 dB | −113.9 dB | 32 Hz – 4699 Hz | 33.3 ms | 0 |
| `modelled_8x10_edge.wav` | −22.95 | −50.04 | −0.000 dB | −108.1 dB | 34 Hz – 2172 Hz | 34.8 ms | 0 |
| `modelled_1x15_vintage.wav` | −26.47 | −53.28 | −0.000 dB | −69.0 dB | 34 Hz – 1804 Hz | 63.0 ms | 0 |
| `modelled_4x10_horn.wav` | −20.05 | −48.54 | 0.000 dB | −76.0 dB | 37 Hz – 3079 Hz | 49.4 ms | 0 |

No file contains a clipped sample, a non-finite sample, or a DC offset above
1e-4. `tests/FactoryIRTests.cpp` re-measures every bundled asset through the
plugin's own decoder and convolution path, so a regression fails the build
rather than the release.

## Release rules

Adopted with the bundled-IR resolution model (issue #111, following
basilica-audio/Nave's curation decision, Nave#48):

- **Rename freely.** A cabinet's identity is its model id (`bass-810-cone`,
  …), which lives in `manifest.json` and in
  `CryptaAudioProcessor::getFactoryIRAssetTable()`. Presets never resolve by
  name, so a rename changes nothing they depend on.
- **Never retune in place.** Presets resolve by the SHA-256 of the file's
  bytes. A retuned model changes the bytes, so every existing reference to it
  would miss — loudly, which is the designed behaviour, but it turns a
  "voicing tweak" into a breaking change for every preset ever saved with
  that cabinet. A genuinely better voicing ships as a **new** model with a
  new id and a new file.
- **Removal is a major-version break.** Once shipped, a cabinet's digest is
  referenced by user presets forever after. `tests/BundledIrCurationTests.cpp`
  pins the shipped set, so a removal cannot pass review unnoticed.

## Footprint

The bundle costs what this table says it costs, measured from the bytes
actually compiled into the binary — `tests/BundledIrCurationTests.cpp` fails
the build if the figures drift (including when this file itself is edited:
it ships inside the binary too, so its own size is part of the figure and the
test constants must be updated in the same change).

| What | Files | Bytes |
|---|---|---|
| Audio | 4 × `modelled_*.wav` | 49,328 |
| Provenance | `LICENSES.md`, `CC0-1.0.txt`, `manifest.json` | 24,296 |
| **Total** | | **73,624** |

`.gitattributes` marks everything under `resources/` as `-text` so these are
the same bytes on every platform — Git's default line-ending conversion on
Windows would otherwise grow every embedded *text* asset by one byte per line
and make the shipped provenance differ from the committed one (the failure
Nave#48 caught on Windows CI).

## How to add one

1. If it is generated: add the model to `tools/ir-synth/cabsynth.py`, re-run it
   into this folder, and re-run `verify_irs.py`.
2. If it is a third-party asset: verify the licence at the source and archive the
   evidence (the licence page itself, not a third party's description of it).
3. Add the WAV to `juce_add_binary_data()` in `CMakeLists.txt`.
4. Add the entry to `CryptaAudioProcessor::getFactoryIRAssetTable()` in
   `src/PluginProcessor.cpp`, with its licence string and a source field a
   reviewer can check without asking anyone.
5. Add a section to this file.
6. `tests/FactoryIRTests.cpp` fails if the entry does not clear the bar, so the
   build is the last line of defence rather than the review.

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)

# Must be set before the first project() call to take effect.
# CI overrides CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES explicitly for release/universal builds;
# local builds are left at the native architecture.
set(CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET "11.0" CACHE STRING "Minimum macOS deployment target" FORCE)


# JUCE's build tooling (juceaide) and some CMake find-modules it triggers
# (e.g. FindThreads) expect the C toolchain to be available; declaring it
# here at the top level avoids it being enabled implicitly deeper inside
# JUCE's CMake helpers, which has been observed to break Ninja's generate
# step (missing CMAKE_C_COMPILE_OBJECT rule variable).
project(Crypta VERSION 0.4.1 LANGUAGES C CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE "Release" CACHE STRING "Build type" FORCE)
endif()

list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake")
include(cmake/CPM.cmake)

# CPMAddPackage automatically respects the CPM_SOURCE_CACHE environment
# variable if it is set, reusing a shared package cache across builds/checkouts.
if(DEFINED ENV{CPM_SOURCE_CACHE})
    message(STATUS "Crypta: using CPM_SOURCE_CACHE at $ENV{CPM_SOURCE_CACHE}")
endif()

CPMAddPackage(
    NAME JUCE
    GITHUB_REPOSITORY juce-framework/JUCE
    GIT_TAG 8.0.14
    GIT_SHALLOW TRUE
)

# ==============================================================================
# Plugin target
# ==============================================================================

juce_add_plugin(Crypta
    # The trading name, not the legal person. This is the string a host groups
    # plugins by - Logic's plugin manager, Cubase's vendor column, Reaper's FX
    # browser - and the suite ships under one brand. Display only: the VST3
    # class ID derives from PLUGIN_MANUFACTURER_CODE + PLUGIN_CODE alone (JUCE
    # 8.0.14, juce_VST3ModuleInfo.h, VST3Interface::jucePluginId) and the Audio
    # Unit identity triple stays (aufx, Crypta's PLUGIN_CODE, Yvsv), so no
    # existing session is disturbed. See docs/branding.md.
    COMPANY_NAME "Basilica Audio"
    # DELIBERATELY NOT RENAMED to com.basilicaaudio.*, and not an oversight.
    # The bundle ID is how a host recognises this plugin across sessions, and
    # how every preset file ever written names it ("plugin" field). Changing it
    # makes every existing project treat this as a different plugin, for no
    # user-visible benefit - nothing a customer sees flows from it. Recorded in
    # basilica-audio/.github docs/adr/0001-suite-vendor-identity.md.
    BUNDLE_ID com.yvesvogl.crypta

# ==============================================================================
# Embedded assets: M2 preset system factory presets (presets/factory/*.json)
# and the M2 i18n frame's German translation (resources/i18n/de.txt). See
# src/presets/PresetManager.h and src/presets/Localisation.h - both consume
# these purely via BinaryData:: symbols passed in from PluginProcessor.cpp/
# PluginEditor.cpp, never by including BinaryData.h themselves, so they stay
# portable to sibling plugins (see docs/preset-system-notes.md in
# basilica-audio/nave, the M2 pilot this suite-wide pattern was replicated
# from).
# ==============================================================================

juce_add_binary_data(CryptaBinaryData SOURCES
    presets/factory/default.json
    presets/factory/glueAndGrind.json
    presets/factory/subLock.json
    presets/factory/throat.json
    presets/factory/fuzzWall.json
    presets/factory/cutThrough.json
    presets/factory/definitionOnly.json
    presets/factory/cleanLowLoudTop.json
    presets/factory/cabColoredGrind.json
    presets/factory/circuitFoundation.json
    presets/factory/circuitGrind.json
    presets/factory/circuitKnife.json
    resources/i18n/de.txt
    # Suite typography (M3/M6 vector editor, issues #45/#25): EB Garamond,
    # OFL licensed (resources/fonts/OFL-EBGaramond.txt) - consumed by
    # src/gui/BasilicaLookAndFeel.cpp as the single source of every glyph
    # the fully JUCE-drawn editor renders.
    resources/fonts/EBGaramond-Regular.ttf
    resources/fonts/EBGaramond-SemiBold.ttf
    # Factory cabinet impulse responses (issues #21/#81). Every one of these is
    # GENERATED, not recorded: tools/ir-synth/cabsynth.py computes them from a
    # documented analytical cabinet model, so there is no third-party recording
    # inside the shipped binary and therefore no provenance to trace or dispute.
    # Licensing, per-file model parameters, checksums and the measured response
    # of each are in resources/irs/LICENSES.md; the CC0 dedication these are
    # published under is committed at resources/irs/CC0-1.0.txt. Registered in
    # CryptaAudioProcessor::getFactoryIRAssetTable(), guarded by the licence bar
    # in src/dsp/FactoryIRs.cpp and re-measured by tests/FactoryIRTests.cpp.
    # Wave-3 photoreal "composited plate" GUI (see src/PluginEditor.h): the
    # approved empty master plate, the suite control sprites (feathered-alpha
    # crops from approved master renders - provenance in the gui-pipeline
    # scaffold's sprite-library/provenance.md), and the layout manifest that
    # maps every parameter id to a sprite type + plate position.
    resources/gui/plate_crypta.png
    resources/gui/sprite_knob.png
    resources/gui/sprite_selector.png
    resources/gui/sprite_toggle_up.png
    resources/gui/sprite_vu_dial.png
    resources/gui/layout-manifest.json
    resources/irs/modelled_8x10_cone.wav
    resources/irs/modelled_8x10_edge.wav
    resources/irs/modelled_1x15_vintage.wav
    resources/irs/modelled_4x10_horn.wav
    # Provenance travels with the audio (issue #111, adopting Nave's #48
    # curation rules): the licensing bar is a licence committed ALONGSIDE the
    # audio, so a shipped binary carries it too, and a materialised/installed
    # copy can never leave it behind. Consumed by crypta::factoryIrAssets()
    # in src/PluginProcessor.cpp; byte-exactness on every platform is what
    # .gitattributes' `-text` rules and the footprint assertion in
    # tests/BundledIrCurationTests.cpp guard.
    resources/irs/LICENSES.md
    resources/irs/CC0-1.0.txt
    resources/irs/manifest.json
)

# ==============================================================================
# SharedCode: an INTERFACE target carrying the plugin's sources, definitions,
# and library links so that both the plugin targets (AU/VST3/Standalone) and
# the Tests executable compile the exact same code (Pamplejuce pattern, see
# https://github.com/sudara/pamplejuce), avoiding ODR violations between them.
# ==============================================================================

add_library(SharedCode INTERFACE)

target_compile_features(SharedCode INTERFACE cxx_std_20)

file(GLOB_RECURSE CryptaSources CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.h")

target_sources(SharedCode INTERFACE ${CryptaSources})

target_include_directories(SharedCode INTERFACE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src")

target_compile_definitions(SharedCode INTERFACE
    JUCE_WEB_BROWSER=0
    JUCE_USE_CURL=0
    JUCE_VST3_CAN_REPLACE_VST2=0
    # AGPLv3 usage permits disabling the splash screen.
    JUCE_DISPLAY_SPLASH_SCREEN=0
    # Issue #99: juce::dsp's per-call denormal guard makes the render depend
    # on the host's buffer size on Intel, and it is redundant here.
    #
    # util::snapToZero() (JUCE 8.0.14, juce_dsp/juce_dsp.h) zeroes a filter's
    # internal state at the END of every process() call once its magnitude
    # falls below 1e-8, and it is called once per call by
    # LinkwitzRileyFilter, IIR::Filter, Oversampling and BallisticsFilter -
    # i.e. by both crossover splits, the phase-align allpass, the post-sum EQ
    # and every oversampled drive stage. The snap events therefore land on the
    # host's block boundaries: move the boundaries and the state trajectory,
    # and so the output, changes. JUCE_SNAP_TO_ZERO is `#if JUCE_INTEL`
    # (juce_audio_basics/buffers/juce_FloatVectorOperations.h), so this was an
    # Intel-only property - an offline bounce at 512 did not match realtime
    # monitoring at 128 on an Intel machine, while an Apple Silicon build of
    # the same source was bit-exact. Measured before this flag: -75.9 dB /
    # 1.3e-03 peak worst case, agreeing to 0.2 dB between MSVC on Windows and
    # Apple clang on macOS x86_64, which is what ruled out codegen.
    #
    # Denormal protection is NOT removed by switching the guard off - it moves
    # from state-zeroing at call boundaries to the FPU, which is both stronger
    # and free. CryptaAudioProcessor::processBlock() opens with
    # juce::ScopedNoDenormals, which sets MXCSR FTZ|DAZ (mask 0x8040) on Intel
    # and FPCR FZ on ARM for the whole callback and restores the host's own
    # mode on the way out, so every arithmetic result is flushed rather than
    # only the filter state juce::dsp happens to snap. No DSP in this plugin
    # runs outside that scope: processBlockBypassed() is JUCE's default, which
    # performs no arithmetic. src/PluginProcessor.cpp carries a static_assert
    # tying the two together, so this flag cannot be set on a target where
    # ScopedNoDenormals is a no-op.
    JUCE_DSP_ENABLE_SNAP_TO_ZERO=0
)

target_link_libraries(SharedCode INTERFACE
    juce::juce_audio_utils
    # Preset -> IR references resolve by SHA-256 of the IR file's bytes (see
    # src/presets/IrReference.h). juce_cryptography depends only on juce_core
    # and adds nothing to the audio path.
    juce::juce_cryptography
    juce::juce_dsp
    juce::juce_gui_basics
    juce::juce_recommended_config_flags
    juce::juce_recommended_lto_flags
    juce::juce_recommended_warning_flags
    CryptaBinaryData
)

target_link_libraries(Crypta PRIVATE SharedCode)

# ==============================================================================
# Tests
# ==============================================================================

enable_testing()
set(CTEST_OUTPUT_ON_FAILURE ON)

CPMAddPackage(
    NAME Catch2
    GITHUB_REPOSITORY catchorg/Catch2
    GIT_TAG v3.15.2
)

file(GLOB_RECURSE CryptaTestSources CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/*.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/*.h")

add_executable(Tests ${CryptaTestSources})

target_compile_features(Tests PRIVATE cxx_std_20)

target_link_libraries(Tests PRIVATE SharedCode Catch2::Catch2)

# Copy over the plugin target's compile definitions (JucePlugin_* macros etc.)
# so plugin code compiles identically when built as part of the Tests binary.
target_compile_definitions(Tests PRIVATE
    $<TARGET_PROPERTY:Crypta,COMPILE_DEFINITIONS>
    JUCE_MODAL_LOOPS_PERMITTED=1
    # tests/QaGateManifestTests.cpp reads scripts/qa-gates.tsv - the QA gate's
    # declaration of which Catch2 tags make up docs/qa-checklist.md Part 1 -
    # and asserts every tag in it is still carried by a registered test case.
    # A repository file has to be located from the test binary to do that, and
    # the binary's own location moves with the generator and configuration.
    CRYPTA_REPO_ROOT="${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}"
)

set_target_properties(Tests PROPERTIES XCODE_GENERATE_SCHEME ON)

include(${Catch2_SOURCE_DIR}/extras/Catch.cmake)

if(CMAKE_GENERATOR STREQUAL "Xcode")
    set(CryptaDiscoveryMode PRE_TEST)
else()
    set(CryptaDiscoveryMode POST_BUILD)
endif()

catch_discover_tests(Tests DISCOVERY_MODE ${CryptaDiscoveryMode})

cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.24)

# Must be set before the first project() call to take effect.
# CI overrides CMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES explicitly for release/universal builds;
# local builds are left at the native architecture.
set(CMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET "11.0" CACHE STRING "Minimum macOS deployment target" FORCE)

# JUCE's build tooling (juceaide) and some CMake find-modules it triggers
# (e.g. FindThreads) expect the C toolchain to be available; declaring it
# here at the top level avoids it being enabled implicitly deeper inside
# JUCE's CMake helpers, which has been observed to break Ninja's generate
# step (missing CMAKE_C_COMPILE_OBJECT rule variable).
project(Lancet VERSION 0.5.0 LANGUAGES C CXX)

set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 20)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)

if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
    set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE "Release" CACHE STRING "Build type" FORCE)
endif()

list(APPEND CMAKE_MODULE_PATH "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/cmake")
include(cmake/CPM.cmake)

# CPMAddPackage automatically respects the CPM_SOURCE_CACHE environment
# variable if it is set, reusing a shared package cache across builds/checkouts.
if(DEFINED ENV{CPM_SOURCE_CACHE})
    message(STATUS "Lancet: using CPM_SOURCE_CACHE at $ENV{CPM_SOURCE_CACHE}")
endif()

CPMAddPackage(
    NAME JUCE
    GITHUB_REPOSITORY juce-framework/JUCE
    GIT_TAG 8.0.14
    GIT_SHALLOW TRUE
)

# ==============================================================================
# Plugin target
# ==============================================================================

juce_add_plugin(Lancet
    COMPANY_NAME "Yves Vogl"
    BUNDLE_ID com.yvesvogl.lancet
    PLUGIN_MANUFACTURER_CODE Yvsv
    PLUGIN_CODE Lnct
    FORMATS AU VST3 Standalone
    PRODUCT_NAME "Lancet"
    COPY_PLUGIN_AFTER_BUILD TRUE
    IS_SYNTH FALSE
    NEEDS_MIDI_INPUT FALSE
    NEEDS_MIDI_OUTPUT FALSE
    IS_MIDI_EFFECT FALSE
    ICON_BIG "docs/assets/icon.png"
)

# ==============================================================================
# Embedded assets: M2 preset system factory presets (presets/factory/*.json)
# and the M2 i18n frame's German translation (resources/i18n/de.txt). See
# src/presets/PresetManager.h and src/presets/Localisation.h - both consume
# these purely via BinaryData:: symbols passed in from PluginProcessor.cpp/
# PluginEditor.cpp, never by including BinaryData.h themselves, so they stay
# portable to sibling plugins (see basilica-audio/nave's
# docs/preset-system-notes.md).
# ==============================================================================

juce_add_binary_data(LancetBinaryData SOURCES
    presets/factory/default.json
    presets/factory/gentleGlue.json
    presets/factory/deEssStack.json
    presets/factory/transientSnareCrack.json
    presets/factory/mixBussSettle.json
    presets/factory/slowTonalRide.json
    presets/factory/chestResonanceTamer.json
    presets/factory/fastRecoveryDemo.json
    presets/factory/listenCheck.json
    presets/factory/analogWarmthLift.json
    presets/factory/sidechainCarve.json
    resources/i18n/de.txt
)

# ==============================================================================
# SharedCode: an INTERFACE target carrying the plugin's sources, definitions,
# and library links so that both the plugin targets (AU/VST3/Standalone) and
# the Tests executable compile the exact same code (Pamplejuce pattern, see
# https://github.com/sudara/pamplejuce), avoiding ODR violations between them.
# ==============================================================================

add_library(SharedCode INTERFACE)

target_compile_features(SharedCode INTERFACE cxx_std_20)

file(GLOB_RECURSE LancetSources CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src/*.h")

target_sources(SharedCode INTERFACE ${LancetSources})

target_include_directories(SharedCode INTERFACE "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/src")

target_compile_definitions(SharedCode INTERFACE
    JUCE_WEB_BROWSER=0
    JUCE_USE_CURL=0
    JUCE_VST3_CAN_REPLACE_VST2=0
    # AGPLv3 usage permits disabling the splash screen.
    JUCE_DISPLAY_SPLASH_SCREEN=0
)

# Add any extra juce:: modules a specific plugin needs (e.g. juce_audio_formats
# for reading impulse-response files) to this list.
target_link_libraries(SharedCode INTERFACE
    juce::juce_audio_utils
    juce::juce_dsp
    juce::juce_gui_basics
    juce::juce_recommended_config_flags
    juce::juce_recommended_lto_flags
    juce::juce_recommended_warning_flags
    LancetBinaryData
)

target_link_libraries(Lancet PRIVATE SharedCode)

# ==============================================================================
# Tests
# ==============================================================================

enable_testing()
set(CTEST_OUTPUT_ON_FAILURE ON)

CPMAddPackage(
    NAME Catch2
    GITHUB_REPOSITORY catchorg/Catch2
    GIT_TAG v3.15.2
)

file(GLOB_RECURSE LancetTestSources CONFIGURE_DEPENDS
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/*.cpp"
    "${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/*.h")

add_executable(Tests ${LancetTestSources})

target_compile_features(Tests PRIVATE cxx_std_20)

target_link_libraries(Tests PRIVATE SharedCode Catch2::Catch2)

# Copy over the plugin target's compile definitions (JucePlugin_* macros etc.)
# so plugin code compiles identically when built as part of the Tests binary.
target_compile_definitions(Tests PRIVATE
    $<TARGET_PROPERTY:Lancet,COMPILE_DEFINITIONS>
    JUCE_MODAL_LOOPS_PERMITTED=1
    # Checked-in state fixtures the migration tests load from disk (v0.4.0,
    # tests/fixtures/). Passed as a path rather than embedded via BinaryData so
    # that a fixture stays a plain, reviewable file: the whole point of
    # tests/fixtures/state-v0.3.0.xml is that a human can read exactly what an
    # old session looked like.
    LANCET_TEST_FIXTURES_DIR="${CMAKE_CURRENT_SOURCE_DIR}/tests/fixtures"
)

set_target_properties(Tests PROPERTIES XCODE_GENERATE_SCHEME ON)

include(${Catch2_SOURCE_DIR}/extras/Catch.cmake)

if(CMAKE_GENERATOR STREQUAL "Xcode")
    set(LancetDiscoveryMode PRE_TEST)
else()
    set(LancetDiscoveryMode POST_BUILD)
endif()

catch_discover_tests(Tests DISCOVERY_MODE ${LancetDiscoveryMode})
